background.fact: AI is Adobe Illustrator's native artwork format.
An AI document can mix vector objects with pixel images.
Illustrator preserves editable effects, brushes, layers, and transparency in AI documents.
Illustrator 9 changed the AI format in 2000; earlier files used PostScript.
The PDF-compatible saving option includes a PDF rendition alongside Illustrator data.
Designers use AI source files for logos, illustrations, and print layouts.

windows.note: Can read the AI format identified in its format list as Illustrator CS2; rendering is not native Illustrator editing.
Opens native artwork with editable Illustrator objects.

mac.note: Can read the AI format identified in its format list as Illustrator CS2; rendering is not native Illustrator editing.
Opens native artwork with editable Illustrator objects.

linux.note: Its import manual lists AI artwork from Illustrator 9.0 onward; some document features may be unavailable.
Can read the AI format identified in its format list as Illustrator CS2; rendering is not native Illustrator editing.

problems.fact: A program that reads the embedded PDF does not necessarily expose native Illustrator objects for editing.
An AI file saved without its PDF-compatible representation may fail in third-party software.
Opening artwork in an older Illustrator version can cause compatibility problems; Adobe advises matching or newer versions.
Linked images remain external unless Include Linked Files is selected while saving.

background.fact: WMA audio files use Microsoft's ASF container.
The .wma extension distinguishes audio-only material from other ASF content.
Windows Media Audio has standard, Professional, Lossless, and Voice codec variants.
WMA 9 supports variable bit rate encoding.
The media type commonly associated with WMA is audio/x-ms-wma.
WMA serves delivery workflows and sometimes intermediate audio storage.

windows.note: Lists ASF/WMA input and multiple Windows Media Audio decoders.
Imports unprotected WMA audio when its optional FFmpeg library is installed.
Decodes WMA 1, WMA 2, Pro, Voice, and Lossless in its support matrix.

mac.note: Lists ASF/WMA input and multiple Windows Media Audio decoders.
Imports unprotected WMA audio when its optional FFmpeg library is installed.
Decodes WMA 1, WMA 2, Pro, Voice, and Lossless in its support matrix.

linux.note: Lists ASF/WMA input and multiple Windows Media Audio decoders.
Imports unprotected WMA audio when its optional FFmpeg library is installed.
Decodes WMA 1, WMA 2, Pro, Voice, and Lossless in its support matrix.

problems.fact: Protected WMA files cannot be imported through Audacity's FFmpeg library.
WMA import may be missing from Audacity until the optional FFmpeg component is installed.
An application may support one WMA codec but lack another; the extension does not identify the variant.
Audition enables WMA import on Windows only, with DLMS Format Support enabled.

background.fact: VOB means DVD Video Object.
DVD producers store video, sound, subtitles, and menu content in VOB streams.
VOB data is closely related to MPEG-2 program-stream material.
DVD authoring also needs companion IFO and BUP files.
A DVD backup commonly places VOB files inside a VIDEO_TS directory.
DVD subtitle streams can contain bitmap images rather than searchable text.

windows.note: Reads DVD Video media and MPEG program streams.
Opens VOB files and VIDEO_TS disc folders; its input must be unprotected.

mac.note: Reads DVD Video media and MPEG program streams.
Opens VOB files and VIDEO_TS disc folders; its input must be unprotected.

linux.note: Reads DVD Video media and MPEG program streams.
Opens VOB files and VIDEO_TS disc folders; its input must be unprotected.

problems.fact: HandBrake does not process copy-protected DVD sources.
A loose VOB does not replace the full DVD structure needed for authoring.
A player that handles MPEG-2 video may still ignore DVD subtitle streams.
A disc source may contain several titles; choosing the wrong title produces the wrong clip.

background.fact: Apple developed Audio Interchange File Format.
AIFF is an audio wrapper derived from Electronic Arts' IFF family.
AIFF often carries uncompressed linear PCM samples.
AIFF-C extends the family to compressed audio.
AIFF can include named chunks for author, copyright, and annotations.
Professional audio users use AIFF for masters and intermediate recordings.
Common AIFF media-type labels include audio/aiff and audio/x-aiff.
Apple's AIFF 1.3 specification is dated January 4, 1989.

windows.note: Imports most AIFF files, including all PCM variants, without its optional FFmpeg library.
Lists AIFF encoding and decoding support.
Opens uncompressed AIFF and most common compressed variants.

mac.note: Imports most AIFF files, including all PCM variants, without its optional FFmpeg library.
Lists AIFF encoding and decoding support.
Opens uncompressed AIFF and most common compressed variants.

linux.note: Imports most AIFF files, including all PCM variants, without its optional FFmpeg library.
Lists AIFF encoding and decoding support.

problems.fact: AIFF-C compression requires a decoder for the actual encoding; the family name alone does not establish support.
Uncompressed PCM needs more storage than a compressed delivery representation of the same recording.
An AIFF author field can appear in Audition under Dublin Core: Creator instead of a field labeled Author.
FFmpeg does not write AIFF ID3 tags unless that option is enabled.

background.fact: Advanced Audio Coding is a perceptual audio coding family standardized through MPEG.
MPEG-2 specifies AAC in Part 7; MPEG-4 places it in Part 3.
AAC can be carried in MP4, QuickTime, or other wrappers.
A standalone .aac file commonly carries ADTS framing.
The registered media type audio/aac covers ADTS and LATM/LOAS transport.
AAC profiles include LC, HE-AAC, and HE-AAC v2.
AAC is used for streaming audio and end-user delivery.

windows.note: Accepts raw AAC input and decodes MPEG-4 AAC audio.
Includes AAC decoding and an internal AAC encoder.
Imports AAC, including HE-AAC.

mac.note: Accepts raw AAC input and decodes MPEG-4 AAC audio.
Includes AAC decoding and an internal AAC encoder.
Imports AAC, including HE-AAC.

linux.note: Accepts raw AAC input and decodes MPEG-4 AAC audio.
Includes AAC decoding and an internal AAC encoder.

problems.fact: A decoder for MPEG-2 AAC may not understand the MPEG-4 AAC variants.
Changing .aac to .m4a does not replace ADTS framing with an MP4 wrapper.
Decoded AAC can occupy much more space because its stored audio is compressed.
ZIP compression usually offers little extra reduction for AAC streams.

background.fact: Targa is a raster image format associated with Truevision video boards.
TGA supports RGB, indexed-color, and grayscale imagery.
A 24-bit RGB TGA stores eight bits in each color component.
A 32-bit TGA adds an eight-bit alpha channel to RGB.
TGA can use optional run-length encoding to reduce storage.
Video editing and game-development workflows still use Targa images.
ImageMagick groups ICB, VDA, and VST with Truevision Targa.

windows.note: Its official Targa plug-in loads and exports TGA images.
Reads and writes Truevision Targa, including the TGA, ICB, VDA, and VST family.
Opens Targa images and provides Targa save options.

mac.note: Its official Targa plug-in loads and exports TGA images.
Reads and writes Truevision Targa, including the TGA, ICB, VDA, and VST family.
Opens Targa images and provides Targa save options.

linux.note: Its official Targa plug-in loads and exports TGA images.
Reads and writes Truevision Targa, including the TGA, ICB, VDA, and VST family.

problems.fact: Saving RGB artwork at 24 bits removes the space needed for a Targa alpha channel.
A TGA labeled 32-bit normally means 32 bits per pixel, rather than 32 bits for each component.
GIMP's Targa implementation does not preserve every version-2 extension field.
GIMP cannot export full partial-alpha information in an indexed Targa color map.

background.fact: TXT is commonly used for plain text documents.
Plain text does not carry commands for typographic formatting.
The MIME label for plain text is text/plain.
The charset parameter tells a receiver how text bytes represent characters.
Converting rich text to TXT in TextEdit removes styles and formatting.
Plain text does not prescribe a page layout, font, or embedded image arrangement.

windows.note: Opens and edits text files through its file-based editor.
A text editor with Windows builds.

mac.note: Opens, edits, and saves plain text documents.
Opens and edits text files through its file-based editor.
Edits plain text; the project documents Unix and macOS use.

linux.note: Opens and edits text files through its file-based editor.
Edits plain text; the project documents Unix and macOS use.

problems.fact: Choosing the wrong character encoding can make valid text display as incorrect characters.
Saving a styled document as TXT discards its formatting.
Plain text cannot preserve an image or table as a word processor would.

background.fact: SWF is a legacy multimedia format associated with Macromedia and Adobe Flash.
SWF is also known as Small Web Format.
SWF can combine vector graphics, animation, and bitmap video.
Interactive SWF content uses ActionScript as well as a timeline.
An SWF may refer to external media instead of containing every resource.
Registered SWF media types include application/vnd.adobe.flash.movie.
Adobe acquired Macromedia in 2005.

windows.note: A Flash emulator; compatibility depends on the ActionScript features used.
An incomplete Flash implementation for Windows and Linux.

mac.note: A Flash emulator; compatibility depends on the ActionScript features used.
Its documented SWF import extracts video-file audio with DLMS support enabled; it is not an interactive Flash runtime.

linux.note: A Flash emulator; compatibility depends on the ActionScript features used.
An incomplete Flash implementation for Windows and Linux.

web.note: Uses WebAssembly to emulate Flash in a browser; some APIs remain incomplete.

problems.fact: Adobe Flash Player no longer runs Flash content after its end-of-life block.
Ruffle does not implement every Flash API, so an SWF may have graphical or behavioral differences.
Missing external assets can prevent an otherwise intact SWF from behaving as intended.
A video conversion cannot retain ActionScript interactions as executable controls.
